notes:
I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to open the source pages hit the tool's usage limit before any page loaded, and I wasn't allowed any more lookups after that. I didn't read a single page: not Enduring Word, the Bible Hub commentaries (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit), Precept Austin, the NET Bible notes or New Advent.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge, so I haven't written any verse notes. Anything I wrote now would be unsourced.

If you start a new turn, I'll fetch the pages one at a time to stay within the limit, in this order:

1. **Verse-by-verse sources:** enduringword.com (Psalm 113), then the Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on biblehub.com, then preceptaustin.org.
2. **Protestant traditions:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org, biblehub or ccel), Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Matthew Henry, and any Lutheran or Pentecostal pages I can find. I expect most of the tradition differences to show up in v. 6 (God humbling himself) and vv. 7–9.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes; Augustine's exposition on newadvent.org, which will be listed under Psalm 112 because the Latin Bible numbers the psalms differently; and Catholic or Orthodox pages on these psalms' use in worship. The Hallel (Psalms 113–118, sung at Passover) may come up here.

Should I go ahead with that?
